commit.message: Merge f-028-par
Merge f-pr4366
Merge f-028-tools-p1
Merge f-028-eng-p1: engine P1 fixes

Verify and batch windows of up to 16 rows: HIP builds default to 16, narrow builds unchanged

A pipelined group of a layer split is its own window, so 32 slots on four cards were four groups of 8 and nothing
larger could run. The window limit is now a build option (STRATA_WINDOW_MAX_T = auto | 8 | 16; auto is 16 for HIP,
8 for CUDA; SYCL and Metal never set it): include/strata/kernels/window_limits.hpp.

A window of up to 8 rows runs exactly the kernels it ran before (HIP gfx1201 window 8 against main: 3096 of 3097
kernels identical, the other a debug variant; CUDA sm_86 and sm_60: identical or renamed but for a few prefill kernels
NVVM compiles differently, with identical results). The code for 9 to 16 rows is only reached by a wider window:
- per-row arrays of the verifier, the expert source tables (128 / 256 entries) and the remote / peer expert tables follow
  the window; CPU expert jobs stay at 8 tokens (a 9..16-row group is two jobs over the same expert);
- the hyper-connection read is made in slices of 8 rows (its Q8_0 launch would otherwise skip rows);
- the grouped expert kernels run a second pass (SKIP template argument) instead of a 16-entry shared array (51 KB,
  over the 48 KB static limit of CUDA);
- resident_plan runs on 128 threads (up to 8 rows, as it was) or 256; MMVQ, bf16 GEMV, shared expert and MoE combine
  take 9..16 columns only in a wide build; the sm_60 packed path runs wide calls in passes of 8;
- STRATA_P4_TIMING and STRATA_P4_TRACE (include/strata/program/pipe_probe.hpp): opt-in timing and trace of the
  pipelined windows, off unless set.

Tests: src/core/window_limits_test.cpp (target window_limits_test). Real 16-row windows (--batch 64 on four stages,
--batch 16 --batch-groups 1) decode the tokens they decode alone.

Residency-biased routing (STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR) is off by default again on 12 GB NVIDIA cards (#4402)

0.2.7 turned STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5 on by itself on a discrete NVIDIA card of 13 GiB or less. Reports and our own 0.2.7 agent check (4.5 of 10
tasks with it on, 5.6 with it off) tie it to repetition loops and weaker results in long agent sessions, so the owner took the default back
(2026-10-29). With nothing set the engine now routes exactly as 0.2.6 and as STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0 did; STRATA_DEFAULTS=026 is unchanged.

- sm120_series.hpp: route_prior_default() answers 0 on every card; route_prior_resolve() is the pure rule the engine reads (a set value wins on every
  card); kRoutePriorSmallCard stays the 1.5 opt-in value.
- verify.cpp: g_route_prior() uses it; the "on by default on this card" start line is gone.
- Expert settings / Terminal: "Faster answers on 12 GB NVIDIA cards" is now an Off-by-default row that writes STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5; the words
  say it is faster on 12 GB cards but can repeat itself in long agent sessions (nine languages). A 0.2.7 file with STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0 reads as Off.
- Tests: arch_defaults_test (default table over 12 cards x hip x integrated x 026, explicit opt-in values), speed-switches.test.mjs and
  tests/terminal/test_speed_switches.py.
- docs/DETAILS.md: both places that described the 0.2.7 default.

Qwen: the automatic expert cache leaves the reserve it was asked to keep - the ~245 MiB the load allocates after it are priced (#4474)

--expert-cache auto sized the cache from the VRAM free after the weights, less --vram-reserve-mib, the draft head and the other priced
buffers. What the load allocates after the cache and no setting prices - the CUDA libraries the prompt path and the verifier warm up
(cuBLAS handles and workspaces, lazily loaded modules) and the verifier's small buffers - came out of the reserve, so the card ended
about 240 MiB under it: 459 MiB free at --vram-reserve-mib 700 on an RTX A4000 16 GB, 457 MiB on an RTX A6000 48 GB, under the 512 MiB line
the serve check warns about at every request (#2065). Measured with STRATA_TRACE=1: -164 MiB at the prompt path and -80 MiB at the verifier
beyond the draft head, the same with --prefill 512, 2048 and auto, on both cards, and the same on v0.2.6 (so not new in 0.2.7).

auto_cache_slots() (include/strata/core/auto_cache.hpp, tested in src/core/auto_cache_test.cpp) now leaves kLateAllocMib = 256 for it,
unless the card could not keep min_slots (#496) after it, and not under STRATA_DEFAULTS=026. An explicit --expert-cache N and
--vram-reserve-mib N are untouched; the cache is ~100 slots (about 1.8% on a 16 GB card) smaller.

engine: wait up to 20 s for the RAM the expert arena needs, then load with a plainer warning (#4051)

An arena load with 10 GiB available for a 40 GiB arena sent a 60 GiB host into
memory reclaim until it was reset.  The check that is there warns only (a
cgroup limit below the arena still stops the start), and its own example is an
engine that is still exiting.  Before the warning, the load now waits for the
RAM to come back, re-reading it every 0.25 s for up to 20 s, and says so in the
log every 5 s (STRATA_ARENA_RAM_WAIT_S changes the seconds, 0 loads at once).
If it is still short the load goes on as before, with the numbers; below half
of the arena the warning says the whole PC can stall in reclaim and names a
systemd MemoryHigh= as the way to keep one program from taking all the RAM.
Nothing is refused or capped.

detail::wait_for_ram is the loop with its sampler and sleeper passed in, tested
in file_expert_source_test (test_wait_for_ram).  expert_source.cpp passes
g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only against the CUDA 13.1 headers; the engine itself
was not built or run for this change.

Qwen: the PLE residency policy gives its lock back when the lock is what leaves the automatic conversation cache too little RAM (#4518)

The 0.2.7 policy locks the 26.8 GiB PLE table in RAM at start when table + expert arena + 8 GiB fit. What the rest of the load takes
afterwards (KV pools, pinned staging, host buffers of two GPUs) is not known then: on a 128 GB two-GPU PC it left under 5 GiB and the
automatic conversation cache turned itself off, a regression against 0.2.6, which kept 8192 MiB.

When the cache is automatic and the lock came from the policy (not --ple-io ram), the cache is sized first: if unlocking the table
would give the cache more room, PleTable::unlock() hands the lock back (the pages stay cached, the OS may reclaim them), the log says
so, and the cache is sized from the RAM then free. --conversation-cache-mib N and an explicit --ple-io ram are untouched.
ple_lock_blocks_cache() is the decision, unit-tested in src/core/ple_residency_test.cpp.

Conversation cache: parking an idle --batch slot no longer drops the main session's copy with the shared-prefix checkpoint (#4420)

A batch slot's chain holds one checkpoint (the one its admission copied in). park_slot() went through park_source(), whose
drop_superseded() (#342) removes a parked entry when the outgoing chain holds that entry's deepest checkpoint; the main session's
copy of the same conversation qualifies, and the root checkpoint at the end of an agent's system prompt went with it. The next
overlapping request then read the whole 5 K-token prefix again (323 ms in 0.2.6, 4130 ms in 0.2.7).

ConversationCache::supersedes_richer() says when the park would drop an entry that has a checkpoint the slot's chain lacks; park_slot()
then leaves the slot unparked (it is overwritten, as in 0.2.6) and says so. A slot with no such parked copy is parked as before.
The predicate and its test come from the report (shenmintao, #4420).

DeepSeek engine opt-in: the busy experts of a prompt take FP16 GEMMs, not the tiles (DS4_FAT_ROWS=N, default 0: byte-identical path, the packed tiles run exactly as before).  An expert of N rows or more has its weights decoded to FP16 once (iq::f16_rows, the values the tiles multiply), the rows gathered (gather_f16), cublasGemmEx, clamped SwiGLU in FP16 (swiglu_f16); SetArgs skip_ge leaves those experts out of the tiles.  The tiles decode an expert's weights again for every 64 of its rows; a popular expert of a long chunk has hundreds.  Measured on the RTX 5090 with the IST-DAS 2.25 bpw pack, v0.2.7 base, DS4_FAT_ROWS=64: a 13K-token prompt 1,400 -> 1,950 tok/s, a 5.4K prompt 1,065 -> 1,181, decode unchanged (28-33 short, 47-49 warm).  3x V100, Maya-XS: +6-8% on 8K and 32K prompts.  The same products, the sums' order differs: greedy output can diverge after the first rounding (wording equivalent); KL vs the reference 0.276, the stock path 0.285 (the same band, measured on Maya-XS; not yet re-measured on this base).
Merge f-0271-macds (DeepSeek on the Mac) into 0.2.7.1: setup.py keeps the Mac sentence and adds the DGX Spark one for Linux ARM64
SetArgs: the Metal fields exist only in Metal builds (the CUDA/HIP kernels take the struct by value)
SetArgs: the Metal fields go last, so the CUDA/HIP kernels' parameter layout (and SASS) is exactly v0.2.7's

sm_121 (GB10, DGX Spark) speed defaults and the fused prompt tile

nv_defaults.cpp gets an sm_121 table beside sm_86 and sm_60: STRATA_PF_FUSED=1 (fused IQ prompt kernels), STRATA_PREFILL_NVFP4=w4a4
(NVFP4 prompt MMQ with FP4 activations), STRATA_HC_UPMIX=1 (fused hyper-connection read), STRATA_SPEC_COST=1 (cost-aware MTP window).
Measured on one GB10 with paired A/Bs (docs/DGX_SPARK_LINUX.md); a switch the user set is kept. STRATA_SM121_PERF=0 turns the table
off, and so does the 0.2.7 master switch STRATA_DEFAULTS=026. Unlike the sm_86 / sm_60 tables these are not bit-exact (the fused prompt
path and the FP4 activations round differently; 24 of 24 greedy answers were identical), so the start line does not call them exact.

moe_fused_iq.cu: on a GB10 the work-item rule never reached its 128-row tile (the launch average is above 112 rows an expert at every
prompt size), so pick_ww takes the 128-row tile from 65,536 routed rows a launch up (+3% prompt at 16K and 32K; 4K keeps 64).
STRATA_PF_TILE_DEBUG=1 prints the choice. Other parts take the line they took before.

Merge f-dsv41-mac (DeepSeek on Metal) into v0.2.7

The 0.2.7 DeepSeek changes (persistent-grid IQ kernels, int8 rounding batches, hc_mix_split with a block counter, head columns,
chunk-path knobs) are kept; the Metal engine's hooks sit on top of them: every kernel launch is strata_ds4_launch(), the rounding
batch ends in the Metal multi-quantiser dispatch, the head stays at 4 columns a pass on Metal (8 moves the KL), and the macOS
parallel expert prefetch is macOS-only.

batch groups: two NVIDIA cards pipeline by default; the serial group is opt-in (STRATA_BATCH_GROUPS_NV_SERIAL=1, STRATA_DEFAULTS=026)

0.2.1 made a layer split over exactly two NVIDIA cards with --batch and no --batch-groups run one serial group (measured
then on 2x RTX A4000, IQ3_XXS: +12..16%). With the 0.2.7 code the pipelined groups are faster at 2 and 4 streams on
every box and quant measured, so the default goes back to the pipeline.

Measured (tools/serve_load.py, --batch 4, 256 tokens per request, interleaved pairs, total tok/s, pipelined / serial):
- 2x RTX A6000, IQ3_S, all experts in VRAM: 1 stream 101.7 / 101.7; 2 streams 125.7 / 107.4 (+17%); 4 streams 171.4 / 141.0
  (+22%). The v0.2.6 binary on the same box: serial default 104.9 and 137.2, --batch-groups auto 124.6 and 169.6.
- 2x RTX A4000, Q2_0 pack (17037 of 24576 pairs cached, 4 clean pairs): 2 streams 80.2-82.5 / 75.0-75.5 (+7..9%, 4 of 4);
  4 streams 110.8-111.5 / 94.8-95.3 (+17%, 4 of 4); 1 stream 63.6-68.7 / 68.2-70.3.
- 2x RTX A4000, IQ3_XXS (13056 of 24576 pairs cached, 3 pairs): 2 streams 73.2-73.7 / 65.8-66.5 (+12%, 3 of 3); 4 streams
  100.5-100.7 / 82.9-83.6 (+20%, 3 of 3); 1 stream 58.4-60.5 / 60.7-62.6 (serial about 4% faster, 3 of 3).
The single stream runs on the solo path in both; only the A4000s show the 4%.

What changed: batch_groups.hpp has a pure rule nv_serial_wanted(env value, STRATA_DEFAULTS=026). STRATA_BATCH_GROUPS_NV_SERIAL
set to anything but 0 asks for the serial group, an explicit 0 wins over STRATA_DEFAULTS=026, and with the variable unset or
empty STRATA_DEFAULTS=026 gives v0.2.6's serial group. An explicit --batch-groups (a number or auto) still wins. Three or more
cards, AMD builds and --batch-mtp/--adapt-async handling are unchanged. The serial message names the opt-in.

Tests: batch_groups_test (the rule over the env values and 026, two cards pipeline, the existing serial cases). Real engine on
2x A6000 (IQ3_S), no --batch-groups: the engine says "2 groups of 2 slots" / "2 groups of 1 slot"; with 4 and 2 slots, greedy,
greedy+seeded sampled, slots finishing at different lengths and a cancel in the middle of a draft, every slot's tokens equal its
solo decode and the pipelined build's. A long-prompt slot differs from the pre-merge base build in the same way with the flag
and without it (it is the parent's prompt path, not this change).

Not covered: no run on AMD or on three cards; the 4% single-stream cost on the A4000s is measured on one box.
Merge f-027-gh-eng-pm (#4121 MTP drafts in pipelined slots, opt-in STRATA_PIPED_MTP)

layer-major prefill: on by default for a CUDA layer split, STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR=0 and STRATA_DEFAULTS=026 turn it off (#3976)

THIS COMMIT ALONE MAKES THE WALK A DEFAULT. Drop it and the layer-major prefill stays
an opt-in (STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR=1) with the chunk-major path as the default.

Rule (include/strata/core/sm120_series.hpp, pure, tested in src/core/arch_defaults_test.cpp):
- prefill_layer_major_default(hip, stages, v026): on for two or more stages on CUDA,
  off on one GPU, in a HIP build, and under STRATA_DEFAULTS=026 (qwen_defaults_026());
- prefill_layer_major_resolve(env, ...): STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR=0 / 1 (any text
  atoi reads) wins in both directions, over the rule and over STRATA_DEFAULTS=026.
Every decline of the earlier commits stays and runs in lm_prepare as before (HIP,
image prompts, DFlash2 taps, KVA, stop_at_chunk, a pending force_chunk, a peer GPU,
APR / NVFP4 / WMMA / fused layers, STRATA_EXPERT_NIBBLE, no VRAM, no pinned RAM):
such a prompt reads chunk-major with nothing but a log line. When the walk is on by
default (nothing set) the VRAM margin is 512 MiB instead of 96 and the super-chunk
target 32768 tokens (the size measured) instead of 8192; "a short prompt" is not logged.
STRATA_PREFILL_LM_TOKENS and STRATA_PREFILL_LM_MARGIN_MIB still win.

Measured (z440, 2x RTX A4000 16 GB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, experts streamed, 5
interleaved pairs, time to first token, medians): 8K 2.8x, 20K 4.8-5.7x, 32K 5.1-5.5x
faster (141 s to 26-28 s); decode 38.6 vs 38.4 tok/s; needles 12 of 12 found in both
arms. The speed-up is larger than the report's 2x because --prefill auto picks 512-token
chunks there. The first-token KL numbers are in the gate notes (3976-kl.sh).

Not covered: one GPU (stays opt-in), HIP, SYCL, Metal, three or more stages, a card
with more VRAM than the pack needs (where the experts are VRAM-resident and the
chunk-major path has little to re-read).

Merge f-027-gh-eng-d (#3602 #3948 #3638 #3702 #3797 #2409 #3844: audits, fixes and tests)

# Conflicts:
#	src/core/verify.cpp
#	src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu

QFUSE: the fused q8_1 producers divide the way the separate quantiser does; they gave a different code at about one element in a million (#3948)

Problem. #3948: with STRATA_QFUSE=1 the verified text changes and MTP acceptance drops (RTX 3080, sm_86). The report suspected the
group counter or the nat_xq_ offsets of fused_gr.cu; the audit and the new two-group test (previous commit of this stream)
rule those out. What the new test found instead, on an RTX 5070 (sm_120, CUDA 13.0, MSVC), over 10,500 random windows of two groups: in
about 1 run of 400 one q8_1 code of the fused image differs by exactly one from native_quantize_q8_1's, in every mode (group-relative,
window-indexed, direct, graph replay). The scale/sum pair and the other codes agree.

Cause. native_mmvq.cu, which holds native_quantize_q8_1 (the quantiser every consumer of a q8_1 image was written for), is
compiled with --use_fast_math (CMakeLists.txt, the native_* list), so its `amax / 127` and `x / d` are the fast full-range division
(div.full.f32, up to 2 ulp off). fused_gr.cu (the hyper-connection read's tail, gr_up_q32_kernel) and verify_kernels.cu (the GDN
output norm, gdn_q8_1_store) are not in that list and divide with IEEE rounding. roundf(x / d) then lands on the other side of a .5
at the rare element whose quotient is next to a boundary. One changed activation code per ~10^6 values is about one per few
hundred tokens at 80 hyper-connection reads of 2560 values per token: enough to move a near-tie in the verify, and the
draft (which quantises with the separate kernel) disagrees with the verifier a little more often, which lowers acceptance. That
matches the report (acceptance 0.755 against 0.79, different text, and an unchanged text where no draft is made).

Change. include/strata/kernels/q8_1_finite.hpp: q81_div(a, b) is `a / b`, except in a translation unit that defines
STRATA_Q81_FASTMATH_DIV (CUDA device code only, never HIP), where it is the same PTX division the fast-math file gets (div.full.f32).
q8_1_quant and the scale use it. fused_gr.cu and verify_kernels.cu define the macro; nothing else does, so every other kernel,
the separate quantiser and every HIP build compile to what they did. STRATA_QFUSE is off by default on CUDA (it is on by default on
gfx1151, which is HIP and unchanged), so the default path is bit-identical.

Result (RTX 5070, sm_120): gr_parity's two-group window test: 10,500 runs with 1,500 random inputs for each T, all modes, zero
differences (before: dozens); the whole of gr_parity, gdn_parity and gdn_parity with STRATA_GDN_SPLIT=1 pass.

Tests. gr_parity: the two-group test prints the first differing bytes (block, field), and STRATA_GRP_REPS=N / STRATA_GRP_KEEP_GOING=1
repeat it longer and count every failure. gdn_parity: the q8_1 destination check uses its own stream (native_quantize_q8_1 refuses the
null stream, which crashed the test on Windows), unbuffered stdout and STRATA_GDN_PARITY_TRACE=1.

Not covered. sm_86 (the report's card) has not run the new test yet (z440 was reserved for other jobs); the cause is not
architecture specific. The model run (gates/3948-qfuse.sh) is still owed: QFUSE on against off must now be byte-identical, and the
draft counters equal.

Conversation cache: skip a restore only when a card would have to create its copy stream and has no room for it (#2409)

Problem. #2408 / PR #2409: restoring a large parked conversation on a layer split ended the server with a CUDA out of memory
on a later card. The PR checks the free VRAM of every card against --vram-reserve-mib before a restore. Its own review
points out that a loaded card is always below that reserve, so the check would skip nearly every restore on a split (and
on one GPU). It is not ported.

What a restore allocates. conversation_snapshot_restore writes into the session's existing buffers (pools(st), the GDN
state, the indexer tails); refresh_residency only launches kv_stream_reset or copies into the existing ring. The elastic K/V
growth (kvg_ensure) allocates, but only on one GPU. The one thing a restore can create on a card is the calling thread's
private copy stream for it (conversation_copy.hpp private_stream), which it takes from the pool of finished threads when
there is one (#3350). A failed restore is fatal by contract (the session may be half written). So the need is one stream
and one event, and only for a card whose stream does not exist yet (a snapshot loaded from disk, or a restore on a thread
that never copied on that card).

Change. conv_cache.hpp: kRestoreFirstUseMib (64) and restore_fits(free, stream_ready, n, need): a restore is refused only
for a card that has no copy stream yet and less than 64 MiB free. conversation_copy_stream_ready(device) says whether a
card has one. generate.cpp: before the restore, each card of the run is checked; a snapshot that would not fit goes back to
the cache and the prompt is read again, with a log line. A card that has its stream is never refused, however full.
No sample (a failed cudaMemGetInfo) means the restore goes ahead as it did.

Tests. conv_cache_test: the predicate (cards with a stream are admitted at any free size; the edge at the need; no
sample / no cards / no need). conversation_copy_streams_test: copy_stream_ready before and after the first copy, in the pool
after a thread ends, and the measured cost of a card's first copy stream and event (printed; the test requires under
16 MiB, so 64 MiB leaves a wide margin). conversation_snapshot_test: after the first restore, six more restores of two
images leave the free VRAM where it was.

Not covered. The pure predicate and the generate.cpp code build on z440 (CUDA 13.0); the GPU tests are listed in the stream
notes. No model run: gates/2409-restore-guard.sh (a held-VRAM start on a layer split) shows the skip line and an
unchanged answer on the second turn.

Later-card VRAM: audit fixes for failed allocations, the reserve arithmetic as a tested helper, a per-card out-of-memory report (#3638 #3702 #3797)

Problem. On a layer split the later cards are left with very little VRAM after loading (#3702: 68 MiB on the last card; #3638:
268 and 666 MiB, then every batched prompt read of more than ~400 tokens ends non-finite after hours; #3797: the weight arena
fails with 320 MiB free and the message does not say who holds the rest). The window-graph eviction (12b0bce95) and the copy
stream pool (#3350) are in already; this is the rest of the code audit of what is allocated after load.

Audit. The table of every lazy allocation after load (what, when, size, how a failure is handled) is in
phaseA-tests/notes-027-gh-eng-d.md. Bugs found and fixed here, each small:
- verify.cpp capture / capture_batch and mtp.cpp finish_capture: the cudaGraphUpload and its sync were only printed. The
  upload is a warm-up, but a failure (no VRAM) stayed as the thread's pending error and the next kernel wrapper's
  cudaGetLastError ended the engine. The error is now cleared and the first launch uploads the graph.
- verify.cpp capture_commit and mtp.cpp finish_capture: the commit graph called cudaGraphInstantiate directly (no
  eviction of older layouts, unlike the window graphs) and reported the status of the end-of-capture call, which is success,
  so the message read "no error". capture_commit now goes through instantiate_evicting and reports the instantiate's status.
- instantiate_evicting instantiates into a local and sets the member only on success (what a failed instantiate leaves in
  its output is not specified, and a non-null member means "captured").
- prefill.cpp carve: after a failed take of the shared region the sub-allocators had no base and each cudaMalloc'd its
  buffer (hundreds of MiB in all) on the card that had just run out. carve now returns at once; the caller reports the
  failure as before.
- generate.cpp: a failed set_stage_helper / set_peer is reported and the run goes on, but its CUDA error stayed pending;
  cleared.
Found and not changed: relend() re-plans only the first participant (#3638 comment). Read: it runs only from the VRAM
command, which is off on a layer split, so it cannot touch a later stage's loan. Other candidates (ignored cudaEventCreate for
the pipelined fences, unchecked expert copies, cudaFuncSetAttribute flags set before success) are in the notes.

Changes for the report of #3797 and the reserve (#3702).
- include/strata/program/gpu_report.hpp: on a failed weight-arena allocation (first card and each stage) the engine now
  also prints, for every card of the run, the free and total memory and the largest other programs that hold memory on it
  (NVML, loaded at run time; where the driver does not list them it says so). Text only; the failure is the same.
  tests/program/gpu_report_test.cpp pins the text.
- include/strata/program/stage_reserve.hpp: the arithmetic of stage_room (what the split keeps free on a card) moved out of
  generate.cpp unchanged; tests/program/stage_reserve_test.cpp compares it with the old expression over a grid. The file
  also holds a PROPOSAL for a larger window term on a later card (96 MiB + 6 MiB per further window size + 48 MiB, 174 MiB
  for --spec 4) which nothing calls: the default placement is not changed. gates/3702-later-reserve.sh measures it.
- The low-VRAM warning of a later card now adds how many MiB the plan meant to keep free there and how far off that was.

Tests: gpu_report_test, stage_reserve_test (host only, built on z440).
Not covered: no model was run. What the ~700 MiB the plan does not count on the last card is (window graph sets, kernel code
loads) needs the run in gates/3702-later-reserve.sh.

Merge f-027-gh-eng-a (#3622 ARM64 / DGX Spark port, #3806 Gyro-L TQP5/6/7)

# Conflicts:
#	cmake/ggml_tq_overlay_test.cmake
#	src/core/verify.cpp

Gyro-L: read the pair-trellis types TQP5/TQP6/TQP7 (ggml 147-149) on the CPU, CUDA and the MMQ prompt path (#3806)

Gyro-L (agentionai's 50 GiB file) stores its experts as a pair trellis: 128
values per block, a fp16 scale and 64 steps of K bits (K = 5, 6, 7), two
weights per step taken from the first pair of the TQ2_T codebook entry the
step's state selects. The engine refused the file because it did not know the
three type ids. This adds them next to the existing trellis types 144-146
without changing those.

What changed:
- gguf_reader.hpp / tools/gguf_reader.py: names and block sizes (42 / 50 / 58 bytes).
- tq_cpu.*, tq_states.hpp, tq_avx2.cpp: tq_supported / tq_kbits / tq_block_bytes
  for the new ids (the bytes per block are 2 + 8K for the pair layout, 2 + 4K
  for the others), a scalar pair kernel (the reference) and an AVX2 pair kernel
  that is bit for bit equal to it; AVX-512 uses the AVX2 pair kernel.
- iq_kernels.cu: TqInfo, the lane decode (tqp_states8, a byte window), the
  dot product, the decode-once Split, the fp16 dequantizer and the format lists
  for 147-149. They are reached only by a pack that holds these types.
- moe_mmq.cu, strata_ggml_tq_overlay.cmake, third_party/ggml-tq/tq.cuh,
  ggml-common-tq.h: the MMQ prompt path for the three types (overlay
  enumerators, traits, tile loader branch, instances).

spec: a gated request's lookup policy learns from committed rounds only, DraftPolicy choose() unchanged otherwise (#3416)

Problem (KeyanHu-git): the gated proposal needs the choice between the MTP window and a
lookup window to be fixed by the history, not by the draws of the rounds it will verify.
Freezing the policy for the whole request (the first commit) does that, but also freezes
the cost table, so a repeat-heavy request kept the window sizes it inherited. In the
author's diagnostic workload the frozen policy chose mean lookup windows of 5.87 and 3.38
on two repeat requests; with this change 4.31 and 4.05 (from the PR text; not
reproduced here).

Change: the request's copy of the DraftPolicy (source_policy) gets three calls, used only
when gated_proposal is on:
- observe_committed(): the round's accept and probe counts, applied at once. A lookup
  window counts as a probe of its size (tried_), so a size whose cost is only guessed is
  tried kProbes times, not every round.
- defer_cost(end, t, ms): the round's time is held. A time covers the window and the next
  MTP draft, so it depends on every Philox counter up to
  max(p + T - 1, p + a + 1 + S_mtp).
- apply_costs(committed): applies, in order, the held times whose end is behind the
  committed position, with the same update observe() makes (including the STRATA_SPEC_COST
  clamp), in the context bucket the round ran in; delayed_n_ keeps a held time from
  counting as a second probe.
choose() counts the probes as cost_n_ - delayed_n_ + tried_.

Port note: the DraftPolicy on the current tree keeps its costs per context bucket
(STRATA_SPEC_COST), so tried_, delayed_n_ and the held times carry the bucket. A gated
request does not run with STRATA_SPEC_COST (it falls back to the older rule), so its
copy stays in bucket 0.

Default path: unchanged. choose() reads two new terms; on any path that never calls the new
functions tried_ and delayed_n_ are +0.0 and cost_n_ - 0.0 + 0.0 == cost_n_ exactly.

spec: STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1 keeps the confidence gate in the proposal law, opt-in (#3416)

Problem (KeyanHu-git, refs #2028, #2591): with STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1 the default
--spec-min-p gate tests the token drawn from the draft head's distribution q, but the
verifier still judged the draft against the unfiltered q and treated a failed gate as a
plain sample from p. That shifts the output distribution: with p = (0.5, 0.5),
q = (0.875, 0.125) and threshold 0.5 it emits (0.5625, 0.4375).

Change: the gate is part of the proposal. Keep q's mass on the tokens that pass the gate
without renormalising (mu); a draw that fails the gate becomes NULL. An offered token D
is accepted with min(1, p(D)/mu(D)); a rejection and NULL draw from the normalised
positive part of p - mu; a position with no attempted proposal is a plain sample from p.
Serve and the CLI build the same packet (core/gated_proposal.hpp) and give it to the
verifier explicitly (Verifier::set_spec_proposal, sample_tokens_proposal). The explicit
call has no plain-p fallback: an invalid packet row is reported, not sampled around.
STRATA_SPEC_PROB_GATE=top keeps its normalised-q rule.

Default path (STRATA_SPEC_PROB unset): unchanged. mtp.prob() is false, so gated_proposal
is false, the new draft-result argument is null, GatedDraftLimit does nothing,
Verifier::run takes the old branch (set_spec_q clears the measure flag), and the
sampler kernel's old instance is the old code with the new branches compiled out.

default-identity model run is written as a gate script and not run yet.

Decode: opt-in STRATA_MMVQ_IL_PF=1 hoisted-load, exact-integer interleaved GEMV kernels for Q6_K (#3779, #3712)

Problem: the interleaved small-batch matvec (native_mmvq_il) has one weight block
in flight per warp: its four `if (kbx < bpr)` sections each sit behind their own
branch, so on a GA100 (ncu: 432 GB/s on the qkv Q6_K matrix) the loads of a group
are not issued together.

Change, opt-in (every variant is bitwise native_mmvq): native_mmvq_il_pf_kernel
issues every weight load of a group (4 virtual warps x R rows) before any of the
group's dots, with the addresses clamped to the row's last block for a tail, and
with the ring variants the next group's loads before this group's dots. The
per-lane accumulation order is the plain kernel's. P2's forms replace
conversions by exact ones where the value is a small integer: (float)p becomes
p + 1.5 * 2^23 minus 1.5 * 2^23 for |p| < 2^22, and the saturating byte subtract
of Q6_K's codes (0..63, so nothing saturates) becomes two instructions. Q4_K,
Q5_K, IQ4_XS and Q6_K have the variants; Q3_K (the Q2_0 pack's type) keeps the
plain kernel.
- STRATA_MMVQ_IL_PF=1: the measured table (kIlPf_80 / kIlPf58_80: Q6_K only, read
  only when the card is sm_80; on every other card 1 does nothing);
  =2..6: one variant for every type and shape (A/B only, any CUDA card).
- Unset or 0: the plain kernels through the same launch code (the variant argument
  is 0, and the added code is one cached environment read and a switch).
- CUDA only; HIP has no interleaved path.

Conversation cache: opt-in STRATA_PARK_VRAM_MIB=N keeps parked conversations' K/V in VRAM in front of the host copy (#3779, #3712)

Problem: restoring a parked conversation copies its K/V from the host over the
link: 27-107 ms over a PCIe Gen2 x4 link.

Change, opt-in and only with STRATA_PARK_ASYNC=1 (CUDA only): a park also keeps
the whole K/V of its image in a VRAM slot of its own (64 MiB granules, up to N MiB
in all, only while 1.5 GB of VRAM stays free beside it); the background copy to
the host reads from the slot, and a restore of that image copies device to device
from the slot (about 1 ms) without waiting for the background copy. Each K/V
layer carries its own join-and-release token, so any order of destruction is safe
(the layers outlive their image when they are retained for the next park). Under
VRAM pressure the elastic K/V's growth releases every slot and the stage, then
retries once (both growth sites in generate.cpp).

With the variable unset the slot code is not reached: the budget is 0, a restore
finds dev_tag 0 and takes the host path, and the growth sites see
conversation_park_vram_release_all() return 0 and behave as before.

conversation); see the checklist for the reporters' A/B/A conversation check with
